answer: Sybil resistance here rests on binding each agent identity to a non-transferable stake that capital cannot multiply. A new agent must post a bond sized against the rolling delta between identities created and identities that later post verifiable work. Fake accounts widen that delta, so the protocol raises the bond for everyone: a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds, not one. An identity's score also decays unless it emits a genuine pulse of useful tasks, so a canyon of dormant accounts earns nothing. Attacker cost scales linearly; influence does not.
